title: Rice, white, cooked, made with margarine

content.title: About
content.content: White rice, cooked and prepared with margarine, is a ready‑to‑eat side dish. The margarine gives it a smooth texture and a subtle buttery flavor, as well as a modest amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is the most widely consumed type of rice worldwide.
Cooking with margarine raises the calorie count compared with plain boiled rice.
Margarine is often used as a butter substitute in cooking because it is cheaper.
Rice readily absorbs the flavor and aroma of added fats, making the dish richer.
In many cultures, rice with butter or margarine is a traditional accompaniment to meat dishes.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides a quick source of carbohydrates, while margarine adds extra calories from fat.

items.title: Source of vitamin B1
items.content: White rice contains thiamine, important for carbohydrate metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Soft, cooked rice is gentle on the stomach and suitable for diets requiring bland foods.

items.title: Fatty acids
items.content: Margarine may contain vegetable oils rich in polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Reduced glycemic spikes
items.content: Combining rice with fat can slow the rise of blood sugar after a meal.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The mix of carbs and fat makes the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable.

items.title: Trans‑fat content
items.content: Some margarines contain trans fats, which are linked to heart disease.

items.title: Low fiber
items.content: White rice is low in dietary fiber, so it should be paired with vegetables or whole grains.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: A minority of people may react to ingredients in certain margarines.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice with margarine as a side to meat, fish, or vegetable dishes. Enhance the flavor with herbs, spices, sauces, or mixed vegetables for variety.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat until steaming hot before serving. Discard if left at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
